correctness.rationale: Every element has a unique plain/doubled normal form by Nagy Theorem 3. Equality of products yields the exact three-case commutation criterion, which implies the graph decomposition. Maximal prefix chains are the full commuting cliques and are closed under product, including the generator-square corner case. Counting ordered comparable pairs and applying explicit Laplacian join eigenvectors gives the formulas. Independent direct multiplication and rational-nullity checks at n=2,3,4 corroborate all tested clauses; no infinite claims rest solely on finite tests.

value.rationale: The graph of pairwise-compatible elements and maximal commutative subsemigroups are standard structural semigroup invariants. The theorem gives a complete all-rank classification, showing two distinct sizes n+1 and n−1 of maximal commuting subsemigroups, exact multiplicities n! of each, and the complete integral spectral recursion. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or mere reformulation of the established word normal form.
